calls.reason: The leaked chart was not available, and the S-1 shows run rate annualises a trailing 28-day window, which weakens the month-by-month arithmetic. Nothing in the packet reconciles the figures either way, and the credibility doubt is a judgment.

The S-1 quarterly tables show operating expenses falling from about 349% of revenue in Q1 2025 to 239% in Q4 2025 and 135% in Q1 2026. Costs were clearly not rising in step with revenue before Q2, though the Journal chart itself was not seen.
Reporting confirms only that fees were reduced during a May–June ramp-up. No pricing, delivered-capacity or expense records show a preferential deal or an artificial cut to costs.

The S-1 reports $974M of GAAP operating income in Q2 2026, which cuts against the claim. But the SpaceX discount's effect, inference profitability and durability are not measured, so the evidence is mixed.

Anthropic's S-1 shows Q2 2026 revenue up 1,368% year over year while compute costs rose 300%, and the operating-expense ratio was already falling before the disputed quarter. That contradicts costs rising in step with revenue, even though 'in perpetuity' can never be fully tested.

WIRED reported that Anthropic confirmed the $1.25B monthly terms after reduced May–June fees. A later Stocktwits report says the full rate has applied since July, and nothing in the packet contradicts it.
